findings.issue_text: `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:96` — `await prisma.credential.update(...)` added but `prisma` is never imported in the file → TS2304 / `ReferenceError` on every Salesforce client construction.

`packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:97` — `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema)` then `data: { key }`; the helper returns the zod safeParse **wrapper**, not `.data`, so `Credential.key` is persisted as `{"success":true,"data":{...}}`. Google Calendar credentials corrupt on first refresh, for all users including those with sync disabled; irreversible, no backfill.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:5-11` — `[z.string().toString()]: z.number()` / `[z.string().optional().toString()]: z.unknown().optional()` both stringify to `"[object Object]"`; second overwrites first. The "any numeric property is the expiry" behavior doesn't exist; zod strips unknown keys so the sync path retains only `access_token`, discarding `expiry_date`/`scope`/`instance_url`/`refresh_token`. The feature's own happy path is broken/validation is inert.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-21` — sync branch returns a raw `fetch` `Response`, fallback returns the provider-specific object; `refreshFunction: () => any` hides it from tsc. Google (`res?.data` → undefined → `token.access_token` TypeError) and HubSpot (`: HubspotToken` cast, `.expiresIn` → NaN) are broken whenever sync is enabled.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:24-29` — `req.headers[...] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`: with the secret unset/empty and no header sent, `undefined !== undefined` is false → **auth bypass** on an endpoint that writes OAuth credentials for arbitrary userIds. Also breaks permanently if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` has any uppercase char (Node lowercases header keys).

`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98` — unconditional token refresh + `prisma.credential.update` inserted into the connection constructor path, gated by neither `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` nor an expiry check: a network round-trip and credential write per booking/availability call, for users who never opted in.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:25-27` — `refreshTokenResponse.data.refresh_token = "refresh_token"` runs on **both** branches; O365 spreads it over the stored credential, permanently replacing the real refresh token with a literal placeholder. Irrecoverable without full re-auth; no signal, no log.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts` — the team branch checks only accepted membership and `return`s, so `throwIfNotHaveAdminAccessToTeam({ teamId: state?.teamId ?? null, userId })` is only ever reached with `teamId: null`. Any accepted team member can install/overwrite a team-wide credential; the admin gate is dead code.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:36-38,83-90` — `userId` taken straight from the body with no tenancy/ownership scoping: a caller can plant their own Google/O365 tokens into a victim's account, or overwrite a working credential (DoS). The 404-vs-200 split is a userId enumeration oracle.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:57-59` — `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || ""))`: unauthenticated AES-CBC (malleable, no auth tag) decrypt of caller-controlled ciphertext, `|| ""` empty-key fallback, no try/catch, and the result written verbatim to `credential.key` with no schema check. Error-vs-success divergence is a format oracle.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-13` — outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no auth header/signature (asymmetric with the inbound webhook), no scheme validation (http:// ships tokens cleartext), no timeout, no `response.ok` check; anyone who learns the URL can POST an arbitrary `calcomUserId` and receive that user's live access token. Error bodies flow straight into credential storage.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-17` — cascading-failure: no timeout, retry, circuit breaker, or fallback to `refreshFunction()`; a hung sync endpoint stalls every calendar/video refresh path (booking creation, availability).
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:23-90` — no HTTP method guard (GET/DELETE reach the write path), no rate limiting, no nonce/timestamp so a captured request replays forever.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-78` — hand-rolled upsert over non-unique `(userId, appId)`: with multiple credentials per app it overwrites an arbitrary row (no `orderBy`), and two concurrent deliveries both miss the `findFirst` and both `create`.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/{encode,decode}OAuthState.ts:9` — `JSON.parse(req.query.state)` unsigned, unvalidated, no nonce/session binding: no CSRF protection for the rewired callbacks, `state.teamId` is fully caller-supplied, and malformed state throws a 500 out of every callback route.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:78` — `key: keys` is a full replace, not a merge; a partial payload (`{access_token}` only) silently destroys the stored `refresh_token`/`expiry_date`.

`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:90-98` — `key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token }` rebuilds the key from parsed data only; under sync the minimal schema strips `instance_url`/`id`/`signature`/`scope`/`issued_at`, which readers depend on.

`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`: undici/HTTP-2 return empty `statusText`, so this throws on successful refreshes. Use `response.ok`. Remote-controlled string also echoed into a user-facing error.

`packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~258` — the `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", ...)` block was deleted and `safeParse` replaced by a throwing helper: failure mode changed from log-and-degrade to unhandled throw, with the zod error and MS response body no longer logged; `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` is now dead.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:61-91` — no revoke path (a credential revoked upstream stays live forever), no team-credential support (though the same diff makes team credentials first-class), and the update branch never resets `invalid: false`.

Missing verification — zero test files across 30 changed files, for a new public webhook, a new outbound sync call, and rewritten token refresh across 7 apps. Both P0 helper bugs would be caught by one unit test each.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/*` — the credential-sharing-enabled path is unreachable under test: `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is evaluated at module import, so no test can flip it without module-registry surgery. Type checks stay green while the entire sync path is broken.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31` — `.parse(req.body)` (not `safeParse`) unguarded in a Next API route: malformed body yields a 500 + ZodError stack instead of 400.
`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` — non-constant-time secret comparison; `req.headers[x]` may be `string[]` on a duplicated header and is silently coerced.

App slugs scattered as magic literals at each `refreshOAuthTokens` call site (`"google-calendar"`, `"hubspot"`, `"lark-calendar"`, `"office365-calendar"`, `"msteams"`, `"webex"`, `"zoho-bigin"`, `"zoomvideo"`) instead of `appConfig.slug` — self-hosters must reverse-engineer the mapping; typos fail silently.

`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:75-98` — Salesforce uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse` but bypasses `refreshOAuthTokens` entirely, so it is silently excluded from credential sync while still inheriting the broken minimal schema.

`apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:45` + `.env.example` — `|| ""` passes an empty key to AES-256; `.env.example` says "must be 32 bytes" but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`, contradicting itself.

`packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/api/add.ts:17` — `` `/api/integrations/${appConfig.slug}/callback` `` hardcoded to `` `/api/integrations/zoho-bigin/callback` ``; unrelated to the stated intent, de-generalizes working code, leaves a now-interpolation-free template literal.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5` / `parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15` — validation is *downgraded* on exactly the path where input is least trustworthy (operator URL replaces the TLS-pinned IdP), inverting the correct trust posture.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:15-17` — mixed error contract: the helper throws, but every caller still branches on `.success` (`office365calendar:254`, `salesforce`'s `Promise.reject`) — dead code implying a non-throwing contract.
`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/createOAuthAppCredential.ts` — `select: { id: true, members: { select: { userId: true } } }` fetches every member row and never uses it.
`packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:92-94` — `if (!accessTokenParsed.success) return Promise.reject(...)` is unreachable; the helper already threw.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/encodeOAuthState.ts:5-11` — body is an identity round-trip (`JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(...))`) returning `undefined` when state is absent; moved across 8 call sites without addressing it.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: The new webhook handler trusts `userId` from `req.body` (parsed by zod) and performs `prisma.user.findUnique({ where: { id: reqBody.userId } })`, then updates/creates a credential for that `userId` with no additional ownership/tenancy scoping or authentication beyond a single instance-wide shared secret in a header. Any caller who knows/obtains `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` can target arbitrary `userId`s and overwrite/create OAuth credential records (`prisma.credential.update/create`), which can be used to plant tokens or disrupt existing integrations. Additionally, the endpoint returns distinct 404s for missing users/apps vs 200 for success, enabling userId/appSlug existence probing for someone with the webhook secret.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `keys` is decrypted and parsed with `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")))` and then stored directly into `credential.key` without validating the decrypted structure against any schema. The use of `|| ""` is a real empty-key fallback if the env var is unset, and there is no try/catch around decrypt/parse, so malformed ciphertext or non-JSON plaintext will throw and likely produce a 500 response (observable error-vs-success behavior). However, the specific claim that this is "unauthenticated AES-CBC" (malleable/no auth tag) cannot be verified from the diff because `symmetricDecrypt` implementation/mode is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:8-13` — outbound POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with no auth header/signature (asymmetric with the inbound webhook), no scheme validation (http:// ships tokens cleartext), no timeout, no `response.ok` check; anyone who learns the URL can POST an arbitrary `calcomUserId` and receive that user's live access token. Error bodies flow straight into credential storage.

`packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts:5-17` — cascading-failure: no timeout, retry, circuit breaker, or fallback to `refreshFunction()`; a hung sync endpoint stalls every calendar/video refresh path (booking creation, availability).

adjudication.rationale: In `refreshOAuthTokens` (lines ~5-17), when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT && userId` is true, it always does `await fetch(process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT, ...)` and returns that response. There is no `AbortController`/timeout, no retry, no try/catch, and no fallback to calling `refreshFunction()` if the sync endpoint is slow/hung/unreachable. Since `await fetch(...)` can hang indefinitely by default in Node/undici, any caller awaiting token refresh (as added in multiple CalendarService/Video paths in this diff) can stall. This is a concrete behavior observable from the diff, not a style nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:23-90` — no HTTP method guard (GET/DELETE reach the write path), no rate limiting, no nonce/timestamp so a captured request replays forever.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` the handler never checks `req.method`, so any HTTP method that can supply headers/body (or even a GET causing `zod` parse to throw) will enter the same logic path and can attempt DB writes after the shared-secret check. The endpoint also relies solely on a static shared secret (`CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`) with no nonce/timestamp/idempotency mechanism, so a captured valid request can be replayed indefinitely to recreate/overwrite credentials. There is also no rate limiting or throttling visible in this route implementation, so repeated attempts are not mitigated at the application level in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:62-78` — hand-rolled upsert over non-unique `(userId, appId)`: with multiple credentials per app it overwrites an arbitrary row (no `orderBy`), and two concurrent deliveries both miss the `findFirst` and both `create`.

adjudication.rationale: In apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts the handler does a manual “upsert” by calling prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId }, select: { id: true } }) and then update by id or create. This is verifiably non-atomic and can race: two concurrent webhook deliveries can both observe no row and both run credential.create(), producing duplicates if there is no unique constraint on (userId, appId). Also, if duplicates already exist (or are created by the race), findFirst has no orderBy, so it will update an arbitrary matching credential row, which is a correctness issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:78` — `key: keys` is a full replace, not a merge; a partial payload (`{access_token}` only) silently destroys the stored `refresh_token`/`expiry_date`.

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler decrypts `reqBody.keys` and directly writes it to `credential.key` via `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: keys } })` (and similarly on create). There is no validation of the decrypted object’s shape and no merge with the existing stored `credential.key`. Therefore, if the webhook sender provides only a subset of the expected credential fields, the update will overwrite the whole JSON column and drop any previously stored fields (e.g., `refresh_token`, `expiry_date`, etc.). That “full replace, not merge” behavior is directly verifiable in the diff; the data-loss scenario follows from the lack of merging/shape enforcement.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts:86` — `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError(...)`: undici/HTTP-2 return empty `statusText`, so this throws on successful refreshes. Use `response.ok`. Remote-controlled string also echoed into a user-facing error.
matched_golden_ids: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Yes. The candidate flags that the OAuth refresh logic incorrectly validates success by comparing `response.statusText` to "OK", which can be empty or unreliable (e.g., undici/HTTP-2), causing successful refresh responses to be treated as failures. It explicitly recommends using `response.ok`, matching the golden issue about unreliable success detection leading to stale credentials/auth failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:~258` — the `console.error("Outlook error grabbing new tokens ~ zodError:", ...)` block was deleted and `safeParse` replaced by a throwing helper: failure mode changed from log-and-degrade to unhandled throw, with the zod error and MS response body no longer logged; `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` is now dead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)` failure path (which logged the Zod error and the raw Microsoft response body via `console.error(...)`) was removed. It was replaced with `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, whose implementation (added in this diff) throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and does not log the Zod error or response body. This is a verifiable behavior change from “log-and-continue” to “throw”, and after this change `tokenResponse.success` cannot be false (the helper throws first), making the guard `...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data)` effectively redundant/always-true in normal execution.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:31` — `.parse(req.body)` (not `safeParse`) unguarded in a Next API route: malformed body yields a 500 + ZodError stack instead of 400.
matched_golden_ids: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that using Zod `.parse(req.body)` in the API route is unguarded and will throw on malformed payloads, causing a 500 response (with ZodError) instead of returning a 400 Bad Request. adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:25` — non-constant-time secret comparison; `req.headers[x]` may be `string[]` on a duplicated header and is silently coerced.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts` and compares the provided secret via `req.headers[headerName] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. In Next.js/Node, `req.headers` values are typed/behave as `string | string[] | undefined`; with a duplicated header, `req.headers[...]` can be a `string[]`. This code does not normalize/validate that value, so a valid request with a duplicated secret header would be rejected (array !== string). Also, the secret check uses a normal `!==` string comparison rather than a constant-time comparison (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), which is a legitimate security concern for shared-secret verification.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts:45` + `.env.example` — `|| ""` passes an empty key to AES-256; `.env.example` says "must be 32 bytes" but suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`, contradicting itself.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `symmetricDecrypt(reqBody.keys, process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY || "")`, which will pass an empty string as the AES key when the env var is unset; there is no guard earlier in the handler to require `CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, so this can lead to incorrect decryption and/or a security misconfiguration.
